scope: Concrete scene membership API refinement for reviewed successor; no production edits
decision: Separate initial-text construction commits from scene identity binding. Existing PostGraphSceneState(Display) must not silently rerun native constructor effects when binding an existing scene.
proposed_methods: PostGraphSceneState::commitInitialTextItems(): sequentially create/add two owned SfGraphicsTextItem projections with exact native strings and shared Display identity; preserve partial first-item commit if second allocation cannot complete. This commit alone does not qualify complete population.
PostGraphSceneState::qualifyCurrentItemPopulation(string): explicit source/profile coverage over the actual current owned collection, not an observed-empty default. Empty string remains unavailable.
PostGraphSceneState::invalidateItemPopulation(): called at a reached unrepresented mutator; never erase known objects as an invalidation shortcut.

PostGraphSceneState::hasHistogramChart(): require population qualification, traverse actual owned identities, returnfalse only for the supported complete nonmatching collection. Any unrepresented concrete graph constructor/item kind must guard before claiming it was added.
data: Own text objects within the actual scene; text fields and hidden flags are mutable state, not counts.
Initial text commit must be one-shot; scene identity can be rebound without duplicating text items.
Do not expose arbitrary fake graph types or caller-set hasChart Boolean. Real graph constructor/lifetime support precedes graph insertion.
HistogramGraphBinding gains optional secondary scene binding, read at c0d7e0 only after actual histogram.graphOn clear. Null secondary is native items dereference guard.
tests: Existing39/48 behavior unchanged until secondary binding supplied.
Both concrete initial text identities remain after no-match query, including whenhidden.
Changing text strings to SfHistoChart does not make a text object match native SfGraphItem RTTI.
Population invalidation preserves objects and restores exact guard; requalification never recreates objects.
Primary and secondary items are independent; manager.cachedScene is not used as current secondary.
Known complete no-match completes enabledhistogram var0 and processes later live receivers; unknown secondary still retains partial flagclear and stops dispatch.
limitations: Qualified population may be an explicitly declared adapter profile; production fresh-scene coverage is not established by this API.
Text Qt font/metrics/scene callback state remains outside the pure type-query support and must be qualified separately before broader scene parity.
